metaDescription: Five 80V cordless snow blowers and shovels compared on width, pack size and cold-weather ownership, so you can match one to your driveway.
expertTake: The Greenworks 80V 20 inch with the 4Ah pack is the best overall because it combines a proper 20 inch head with a platform that shares packs across many tools. The Litekon 80V 17 inch is the value pick for anyone who wants two packs in the box. Anyone with a long drive, deep snow or a plow ridge should skip cordless and shop a two-stage machine.
introParagraphs: The highest-voltage battery platforms promise gas-like power without the fuel, the oil changes or the pull cord. On a short paved drive that promise holds up reasonably well, especially in light to moderate snow.

But voltage is only a headline. Pack capacity, head width, intake depth and cold-weather behavior decide how long the machine really works, and several listings in this class are shovels rather than true blowers.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 20 in. Brushless Snow Blower with 4Ah Pack
products.description:
This is a brushless 80V machine with a 20 inch clearing path, sold with a 4Ah pack and a fast charger. A brushless motor wastes less energy as heat and has no carbon brushes to wear, which is why it is the sensible baseline for any battery blower.

Its big advantage is the platform. Greenworks 80V packs power a long list of mowers, trimmers and blowers, so the battery you buy for winter has a job the rest of the year. Compared with the older 20 inch listing that ships with a 2.0Ah pack, this kit carries twice the energy per charge, which matters on a drive that takes more than a few minutes.

It is still a hand-pushed battery machine, so it is best on paved surfaces with light to moderate snow. Expect to take smaller passes when snow is wet, and consider a second pack if your drive is long. Keep the pack indoors between storms and dry the auger housing after use.
products.bestFor: A mid-size paved drive for owners of the Greenworks 80V tool line.

4Ah pack and fast charger ship together

products.badge: Best for Packs You Already Own
products.name: Greenworks 80V 20 in. Brushless Snow Blower with 2.0Ah Pack
products.description:
This listing shares the 20 inch brushless head with the pick above but ships with a smaller 2.0Ah pack. Half the capacity of the 4Ah kit means roughly half the working time per charge, so it suits a short drive or a walkway.

The listing highlights compatibility with more than 75 tools on the 80V platform, which is where this kit makes sense. If you already own bigger 80V packs, this is effectively a way to get the machine at a lower entry point and use the packs you have.

The tradeoff is that the included battery is the smallest in this lineup. Plan to buy a larger pack soon if you do not already own one, and keep it indoors between storms. On a deep-cold morning the small pack will fade first, so keep it warm indoors until the moment you start. Compared with the 17 inch Litekon, which carries two 4.0 Ah packs, this kit simply holds far less energy out of the box.

products.name: Litekon 80V 17 in. Brushless Cordless Snow Blower
products.description:
The Litekon is a shovel-style machine with a 17 inch brushless head, sold with two 4.0 Ah packs and a charger. Two packs in the box is the key advantage, because you can run one while the other charges.

Its 17 inch path is narrower than the 20 inch Greenworks, so it needs more passes on a drive, but it is lighter and easier to carry up steps. Compared with the 12 inch Greenworks shovel it clears roughly forty percent more width per pass.

It is a newer brand than Greenworks, so check parts and pack availability before you rely on it long term. Store the packs indoors, dry the housing after use, and treat it as a capable light-to-moderate snow tool. Keep the second pack charged indoors so a swap is ready when the first one fades. It pairs well with a wheeled blower if you also face a long drive.
products.bestFor: Small to mid drives where two packs in the box matter.
pros: Two 4.0 Ah packs and charger included
17 inch path with brushless motor
Light enough to carry up steps
Stores easily in a closet
cons: Newer brand with less parts history

products.name: POXURIO 80V 17 in. Cordless Snow Shovel Blower
products.description:
The POXURIO matches the Litekon on width at 17 inches and lists the same two 4.0 Ah packs, but it states an optimal depth of just 6 inches. That figure is a useful honest limit: this machine is for light accumulations, not deep drifts.

A stated throw of up to 30 feet is generous for the class, though it assumes light snow. The listing describes a lightweight build that anyone in the household can lift, which is its real selling point.

Compared with the 20 inch Greenworks it offers less depth and width, so it is a second tool for steps and walks more than a primary driveway machine. Keep the packs indoors and clear often so snow never piles beyond its limit. Because the depth limit is only 6 inches, clear during the storm instead of waiting for it to finish. The stated throw is a light-snow figure and will shrink in wet snow.
products.bestFor: Frequent light-snow clearing of steps and short drives.
pros: Stated throw up to 30 feet
Two 4.0 Ah packs with fast charger
Light build anyone can lift
17 inch brushless head
cons: 6 inch optimal depth limits heavy snow

products.name: Greenworks 80V 12 in. Brushless Snow Shovel with 2.5Ah Pack
products.description:
The Greenworks shovel is a 12 inch brushless tool with an 8 inch clearing depth, an LED light and a directional vane control. It is sold with a 2.5Ah pack and a fast charger, enough for steps, decks and short paths.

It is designed for medium snow on small areas, and the listing says it can move heavy, wet or packed snow. Against the 17 inch Litekon and POXURIO it is much narrower, so it is a precision tool, not a drive clearer.

Its value is that it shares the 80V platform with the 20 inch machines, so the same packs run both. Keep it as the tool for stairs and let a wider machine handle the drive. Its LED light is a practical bonus for early mornings and late evenings. Expect to make many short passes, so do not buy it as a primary machine for a full drive.
products.bestFor: Steps and decks for existing Greenworks 80V owners.
pros: LED light for pre-dawn clearing
Directional vane control on the head
Shares the Greenworks 80V pack family
Light enough to carry up steps
cons: 12 inch path means many passes on a drive

buyingCriteria.explanation: A wheeled blower like the 20 inch Greenworks clears a wide strip and rolls rather than being carried. A shovel-style tool like the 17 inch Litekon or POXURIO or the 12 inch Greenworks is lighter and better for steps. The mistake is buying a shovel for a full driveway. Choose by area, not by marketing name. The 20 inch Greenworks is the only wheeled machine in this lineup, while every other pick is a shovel-style tool that you carry or push. Think about how long you want to stand clearing snow before you choose the size.

Energy is amp-hours times volts. The Greenworks 20 inch ships with either a 2.0Ah or a 4Ah pack, while the Litekon and POXURIO ship two 4.0 Ah packs. A buyer with a long drive should favor two packs or budget for a spare. One small pack runs out before most drives are done. The 12 inch Greenworks shovel includes a 2.5Ah pack, which is enough for steps but not for a drive. A spare pack on the charger indoors doubles your working time for the cost of one battery.

Width sets passes and depth sets how tall a drift the head can take. The 20 inch Greenworks is widest here, and the POXURIO states an optimal depth of only 6 inches. Choosing on width alone is a common error, because a narrow, shallow head quickly becomes the limit in a big storm. The Litekon and POXURIO share a 17 inch width but differ in how they describe their working depth, so read the listing before assuming they behave the same in a heavy storm.

The Greenworks 80V line lists more than 75 compatible tools, so packs bought for winter keep working in summer. A newer brand like the Litekon or POXURIO has fewer other tools, which matters if you want to reuse the batteries. Pick the platform you will actually use year round. That tool breadth also helps resale and replacement, since a widely shared pack is easier to find years later.

Lithium cells lose capacity quickly near 0 F, so a pack that runs a full session in a garage runs far shorter on a deep-cold morning. Store packs indoors and insert them just before use. A jammed auger can also trip thermal protection, so take smaller passes in heavy snow. Keeping a spare pack warm in the house and rotating it in when the working pack fades is the simplest cold-weather habit.

Single-stage style heads scrape the surface and suit smooth pavement, not gravel. The lightweight shovels store easily, while the 20 inch machine needs floor space. Check your surface first, since gravel points toward a two-stage gas machine instead. Expansion joints and rough concrete also wear the rubber edge faster than smooth asphalt does, so expect to replace it sooner on rough surfaces.

specDecoder.meaning: Amp-hours show how long a pack feeds the motor. More Ah means longer runtime and a heavier pack.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Litekon and POXURIO ship two 4.0 Ah packs while the 12 inch Greenworks ships one 2.5Ah.

specDecoder.meaning: This is how wide a strip the head cuts per pass. It sets how many passes a drive needs.

specDecoder.meaning: Stated throw assumes light dry snow. Wet snow and cold packs cut it sharply.

howWeEvaluated.title: Clearing capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated width and depth against likely jobs. Widths run from 12 inches on the Greenworks shovel to 20 inches on the Greenworks blower. Machines whose size fit the job they target ranked higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery energy
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at pack count and capacity, from one 2.0Ah pack on the older Greenworks kit to two 4.0 Ah packs on the Litekon and POXURIO. Kits with enough energy for a real job scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cold-weather practicality
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on how lithium behaves in freezing air and owner feedback patterns, we favored kits with easy pack removal and spare packs. We did not claim measured results.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed brand track record and tool breadth. Greenworks lists 75+ compatible tools while Litekon and POXURIO are newer. This is based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns.

howWeEvaluated.title: Job fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Each machine was matched to a realistic job from steps to a mid-size drive. The 12 inch Greenworks fit steps best and the 20 inch Greenworks fit a drive best. Machines pushed beyond their limits were flagged.

cards.label: Blower
cards.text: The 20 inch Greenworks machines roll on wheels and clear a wide strip. They suit a real drive and moderate snow.

cards.label: Shovel
cards.text: The Litekon, POXURIO and 12 inch Greenworks are lighter and easier to carry. They suit steps, decks and short walks.

howToChoose.note: Pick the blower for a drive and the shovel for steps.

rows: Run one while the other charges

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Choose a machine with easy pack removal and a spare pack, so you can keep one warm indoors and swap when the working pack fades.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Litekon and POXURIO ship two packs, which makes them easier in the cold than the single-pack Greenworks kits.

howToChoose.note: Do not store packs in an unheated shed.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a mid-size drive and own other 80V tools. The Greenworks 20 inch with the 4Ah pack gives the widest head on a shared platform.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clear steps or a short walk. The POXURIO or the 12 inch Greenworks handles that without paying for width you will not use.

maintenance.why: Cold storage drains capacity and shortens pack life. Warm packs also deliver more power at the next start.
Wet snow refreezes into ice that jams the auger. A quick wipe prevents a stuck start.
A worn rubber edge clears poorly. Replace it before the metal touches pavement.
Lithium packs last longer stored partly charged. Top up once or twice in the off-season.
Vibration loosens hardware over time. A quick tightening prevents lost parts.

faq.a: Not automatically. Capacity and head design matter as much as voltage. A 20 inch 80V machine with a 4Ah pack is stronger than a shovel with a small pack, but neither replaces a two-stage gas machine. Judge a kit by its total amp-hours and the head it drives rather than by the voltage printed on the box.

faq.q: How much should I budget for an 80V kit?
faq.a: Batteries are the biggest cost, so favor kits that include them. The Litekon and POXURIO ship two packs, while the Greenworks kits ship one. Bare-tool listings only make sense if you already own packs.

faq.q: How long will an 80V snow blower last?
faq.a: Motors and augers rarely fail first. Battery packs are the consumable, and cold storage speeds their decline. Keep them indoors for the longest life.

faq.q: Does a shovel work as a driveway machine?
faq.a: Only for light snow on a short drive. The 17 inch Litekon and POXURIO need many passes, and the 12 inch Greenworks needs more. A wheeled 20 inch blower is the better driveway tool. Use a shovel as a second tool for steps and walks.

faq.q: Is it safe to clear a jam by hand?
faq.a: No. Always remove the battery and use a clearing tool, because the auger can move unexpectedly.

faq.q: Can a cordless machine handle gravel?
faq.a: Not well. These heads scrape the surface and can throw stones. Gravel calls for a two-stage machine with adjustable skid shoes.
